newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures crash through support levels.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures crash through support levels.

text.p: IPE Brent futures crashed through key support and shed more than $1.20 a barrel in frantic business in the last hour of business as bearish sentiment took hold of a jittery market.
January Brent traded $1.29 a barrel lower at 1941 GMT, registering one of the biggest single day drops in recent months after going through two support levels at $22.49 and at $22.38 a barrel.
The next support level is seen at $21.80 a barrel.
"It's coming down because we have gone through the earlier low," a floor broker said.

The market's bearish tone was set early in the day when API data showed an unexpected build in middle distillates, which punched the first hole in the market. Then came confirmation that Iraqi crude was flowing in earnest after Tuesday's glitches.
"It's down on a combination of the APIs and Iraq," a floor trader said after the first stops went off below $22.60 a barrel in the afternoon session.
Traders said although the Iraq/U.N. oil-for-food deal had been largely priced into the market, it was still causing jitters.
Turkey's state-run Anatolian news agency said 350,000 barrels per day of crude were expected to be pumped from Iraq to the Turkish terminal of Ceyhan.

Traders said bearish API data -- which showed a one million barrel build in heating oil stocks in the United States, including a 665,000 million barrel gain in the key East Coast area -- helped accelerate the downtrend in place since the end of last week.
But many players said that a downward correction had been on the cards for both Brent and gas oil following last week's rally.
"Iraq and the APIs are part of the story," said one trader. "But I think last week's gains were overdone so I'm not surprised to see it coming off a bit."
Gas oil was similarly bearish. December gas oil, which expires on Thursday, fell $10.25 a tonne to close at $203 a tonne while the January contract was $9.75 off at $204.75 a tonne.
